ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde account review for a false arrival confirmation; note that the tap was taken 1000 m from the pickup with 0 s inside the 200 m radius [F5][F1][NS-2][NS-7].
ruling.reasoning:
The case is a driver-side cancellation with a no-show claim, so it enters through NS-0 and is decided by NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. The driver signalled arrival by an in-app "I'm Here" tap at 22:37:20, so NS-1(i) is satisfied, but the trace records and the GPS confirm the tap was made 1000 m from the pickup point [F5][F3][NS-1].

NS-1(ii) fails: at the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 1000 m from the pickup, and his closest approach for the entire trip was 873 m at 22:36:00 — never inside the 200 m pickup radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) also fails: after the tap he spent 0 seconds within 200 m of the pickup and instead stood stationary 1000 m away for the full 5 minutes 22:37:00–22:42:00 before cancelling at 22:42:00, so no continuous 3-minute-plus wait at the pickup point ever occurred [F5][F2][F3][NS-1].

The platform's own timeline corroborates this: driver_arrived_at is null — no arrival at the pickup point was ever recorded [F4][NS-1]. The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by these system records, which prevail over statements, and so cannot establish a no-show [F12][F5][F2][NS-1]. The rider's chat at 22:38 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?") matches the GPS showing the driver stationary 1000 m away, so the rider was present and ready [F9][F8][F2][NS-2].

Since neither NS-1(ii) nor NS-1(iii) is met, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee does not stand and the whole of it is refunded: the fare record shows exactly $6.61 charged with a 1.0× surge (no surge element to adjust), and NS-7 fixes the voucher form [F6][F7][F3][NS-2][NS-7]. The amount is the cancellation fee itself, $6.61, with no partial measure available because no limb of NS-1 holds [F6][NS-2].

Separately, the driver tapped "I'm Here" while the GPS placed him 1000 m outside the pickup area, which NS-2 treats as abuse of the cancellation/waiting button and requires an account flag for [F5][F1][NS-2]. The flag rests on that record plus the driver's profile of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (which may only support the additional action, never decide the case itself) [F17][NS-2][RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: The fee was charged on the driver's own arrival signal, not on facts: the tap was made 1000 m from the pickup point and the platform never recorded an arrival, so the NS-0/NS-1 precondition the driver assumes is exactly what the record denies [F5][F4][NS-0][NS-1].

Light rain of 1.8 mm with no speed-band and no incident record for the optimal route explains nothing and is not a reasonable-cause record under RD-4; NS-1 allows no weather excuse for the arrival requirement [F15][F13][F14][F1][NS-1][RD-4].

The rider's request for an account review is granted in part, but not on the RD-6 'repeated upheld deviation' branch: RD-6 is a route-deviation clause and this case is a no-show, so the flag rests on NS-2's abuse-of-cancellation-button limb — the tap taken 1000 m outside the pickup radius [F5][F1][NS-2][RD-6].
